summary: This video demonstrates an advanced coastal landscape post-processing workflow centered on cloning to blend two different background compositions, then expanding the scene with warp tools, and layering dynamic color and light to simulate a dramatic sunset. The presenter walks through multi-stage adjustments: from initial clone-blend and perspective extension to sky and light treatment, HDR-like texture work, noise management, and meticulous color grading. The narrative also contrasts a field marine-layer scenario with post-processing results, showcases both color and black-and-white approaches, and emphasizes gradual, iterative shaping of light, depth, and texture to guide the viewer’s eye through the scene.

sections.title: Background blend with clone-stamp alignment
sections.description: Demonstrates using the clone stamp to move and seamlessly blend a different background into the image. The presenter notes the difficulty of predicting the exact starting point and emphasizes previewing multiple iterations to assess whether two compositions merge convincingly.

sections.title: Extending the frame with warp tools
sections.description: Introduces widening the scene by applying perspective warp (described as using four squares to pull out corners) and then cropping the top. This is followed by a quick mention of puppet warp to adjust structural alignment.

sections.title: Lighting direction and sky adjustments
sections.description: Shifts the image toward sunset lighting as a design choice rather than just color. The dehaze tool is used to recover sky detail, with planned adjustments to shadows and highlights. The presenter notes the need for two versions of the sky treatment to manage a bright spot and maintain believable lighting direction.

sections.title: HDR-like texture and dynamic range expansion
sections.description: Returns to Camera Raw for expanded dynamic range, desaturation tweaks, and a plan to push whites and blues. The speaker describes applying an HDR-like texture to water via multiple passes and references Photomatix-like tonemapping, but stresses incremental application to avoid overdoing the effect.

sections.title: Noise control and edge handling
sections.description: Focuses on reducing noise—especially in bright sky areas—while preserving necessary detail on the water. Includes techniques like using history/inverse history brushes to revert selective noise reductions and addressing edge halos caused by prior adjustments.

sections.title: Color grading and diffusion to simulate sunlit atmosphere
sections.description: Explains layering color toward the light source with careful diffusion and dodge/burn work. The workflow includes LAB workflow, RGB tweaks, and split-toning to simulate warm sunset light while maintaining believable shadows, followed by refinements to foreground and waves.

sections.title: Foreground integration and final balancing (and marine-layer caveat)
sections.description: Describes merging darker foreground with a lighter sky to maintain an eye path through the frame. The presenter discusses the marine layer’s role in enabling the scene and demonstrates additional color work to harmonize foreground with the background, concluding with a strong, balanced result.

sections.title: Black-and-white workflow and post-processing practice
sections.description: Demonstrates a black-and-white pass using only dodge and burn tools to create depth and tonal separation. The instructor uses this segment to teach tonal shaping skills in a simplified palette and discusses how color can later be reintroduced if desired.
